content:
Here is the English translation of this passage from Homer's *Iliad* (Book 19, lines 184-197):

Then in turn Agamemnon, lord of men, addressed him:
"I rejoice, son of Laertes, to hear your speech;
for you have gone through all things properly and recounted them well.
These things I am willing to swear, and my heart commands me to do so,
and I will not swear falsely before the god. But let Achilles
remain here for the time being, though he is eager for battle;
and let all the rest of you remain gathered together, until the gifts
come from my hut and we cut trustworthy oaths.
And to you yourself I give this command and order:
choosing the best young men of all the Achaeans,
bring the gifts from my ship, all those which
yesterday we promised to give to Achilles, and bring the women too.
And let Talthybius quickly throughout the broad army of the Achaeans
prepare a boar to sacrifice to Zeus and to the Sun."

This passage shows Agamemnon responding positively to Odysseus's counsel, agreeing to make the promised restitution to Achilles and perform the necessary ritual oaths before battle resumes.
